payload.claim: The acceptance criterion requires that file contents a finding is anchored against come from the critic cell's tree, not the implementer's — and `read_head=lambda path: worktree.read_at_head(critic_container, path)` at line 1807-1809 is the line that is supposed to guarantee it. But no test in this diff (or elsewhere in tests/test_session.py) ever scripts a finding whose line falls outside a diff hunk, so `anchor()` never actually calls `read_head` in any of the four new tests — `anchor([], ...)` short-circuits on an empty findings list, and `_is_anchored` only calls `read_head` when a finding's line is not already inside a hunk. `test_the_critic_reads_the_tree_rebuilt_from_the_exported_patch`'s own assertion, `cell.read_head_containers == [] or set(cell.read_head_containers) == {critic_exports[0]}`, is trivially satisfied by the empty-list branch regardless of which container `read_head` is wired to. Swapping `critic_container` for the implementer's own `container` on that line — the exact regression this spec exists to prevent (items 2, 89, 102, 103) — leaves every gate and every test green.
